title: Durable derivation before online graph writes
finding: Confirmed: deque jobs and pending edges are process-local; take_edges clears before downstream acknowledgement; overflow removes oldest batches. Raw turns surviving is not equivalent to derived work surviving.
solution: Persist membership, source versions, attempts, leases and result/outbox state. Use at-least-once execution with idempotent visible effects, then acknowledge. Preserve replayable raw inputs. Put caps on backlog age and size; coalesce without dropping evidence.
gate: Faults after inference, after each deposit, before acknowledgement, on restart and during forget must not lose eligible inputs or duplicate visible effects. Model calls can repeat; do not promise exactly-once inference.

title: Citations do not prove entailment
finding: Confirmed: facts pass a normalised substring check; edges only need valid line indices. A matching quote may support a different person, polarity or relationship.
solution: Store evidence spans per assertion and per endpoint, with resolved aliases and source role. Validate numbers, units, qualifiers, polarity and entity binding; retain uncertain assertions without promoting them to positive facts. Use semantic adjudication selectively for ambiguity.
gate: Labelled multilingual and cross-domain precision/recall, including short valid quotes, pronouns, paraphrases and misleading common-word spans. Reject a rigid minimum-span or literal-endpoint rule as sufficient proof.

title: Schema needs consumers, not just a shorter prompt
finding: Confirmed: current fact deposit ignores speaker/subject/confidence but uses persons/location/topic. Edge confidence affects weights. Proposed fact/mode/neg/until need explicit consumers.
solution: Define a versioned assertion envelope; compile optional graph edges from it. Keep literal-valued, list-valued and n-ary facts without forcing fake entity nodes. Carry assertion source, modality and negation through storage, retrieval and answer generation. Unknown enum values fail visibly.
gate: Every emitted field has a storage and read consumer or is explicitly transient. Round-trip fixtures preserve negation, attribution, lists, quantities, event roles and temporal precision.

title: Separate utterance, ingestion and event time
finding: Confirmed: window fact date uses _fact_date with a window fallback; episode deposit uses the first record date. Coarse precision must not imply exact day one.
solution: Carry recorded_at, source timestamp and effective event interval with precision and uncertainty. Store future plans as plans. Resolve relative dates against the cited utterance. Keep unknown dates unknown. State changes require effective-time semantics as well as observation history.
gate: Backfilled history, month/year-only dates, future plans, late corrections, multiple source dates and start/end duration joins. Do not replace all state ordering with utterance time.

title: Edge identity must distinguish occurrences and state returns
finding: Confirmed: base key omits kind; dated event variant uses day and numerals. Existing key short-circuits before the conflict ladder.
solution: Version keys and separate assertion identity, event occurrence and semantic deduplication. Same triple is not necessarily the same event. Preserve A→B→A states. Use source occurrence evidence plus event resolution; re-mentions can support one event rather than create duplicates. Define migration and old-key aliases.
gate: Repeated same-day events, repeated mention of one event, state/event same triple, A→B→A and replay of an old-key store. No duplicated facts on migration.

title: Extracting the graph writer is a real refactor
finding: Confirmed: emit is a closure in a namespace sweep with captured state and counters. Calling the entire sweep per batch would repeat broad scans.
solution: Separate pure edge decisions from persistence and sweep orchestration. Add indexed lookups, a bounded incremental entity cache, namespace locking, live-parent checks and transactional outbox/projection recovery.
gate: Characterisation equivalence for existing graph behaviour; scaling tests across namespace sizes; races with erase, updates and simultaneous sleep. Estimate effort after this design, not from moving a function.

title: Cache lineage must survive restart
finding: Risk from code reading, not reproduced: reply-to-source membership is process-local; persistent cache backends can outlive it. A future KNOWN/context input also changes cache identity.
solution: Scope cache by tenant, source IDs/versions, prompt/schema/model, all input blocks and derivation policy. Persist reverse lineage or validate cached dependencies on use. Tombstones and generation checks prevent stale publication after forget.
gate: Process restart with persistent cache, cross-tenant identical text, altered KNOWN input, changed prompt, forget during inference and hard erase. Check absence of retained payloads, not only absence of search hits.

title: Fix packing separately from budget-share experiments
finding: Confirmed: oversize item after a selection breaks packing; first selected item can exceed the budget when no fit stage applies. Fixed 60/20/10/10 shares are unmeasured.
solution: Skip oversize candidates and continue; define truncation/fallback for the first item, count headers and provenance, then enforce final reader-token budget. Test dynamic shares with unused-capacity redistribution separately.
gate: Adversarial long-first/long-middle fixtures, exact total prompt tokens and source integrity; paired category outcomes at equal budget. Token limit compliance is necessary but not evidence of answer improvement.

title: Three gaps are partly implemented
finding: Confirmed: episode summary exists but _store_episode keeps title+narrative. facts/facts_graph mode does not ask for episode summary. rerank_context and facts_to_sources already exist as settings.
solution: Describe remaining work as summary persistence/attachment and bounded integration of existing rerank/lifting features. Store summary once with a pointer, preserve direct evidence, deduplicate parent windows.
gate: Same evidence coverage with fewer tokens; no duplication or stale summaries. Compare enabled existing configuration before proposing a replacement.

title: Token and latency claims need a reproducible manifest
finding: Confirmed arithmetic: 2.7s / 55–210ms is about 13–49× call cost, not uniformly 50×. The latency study used a different completion workload. Prompt v1 and v2 differ.
solution: Record rendered prompt hash, actual tokenizer/template, prefix-cache state, input/output tokens, retries and queue delay. Compare end-to-end p50/p95 and freshness at matched load. Keep 309/353/958 as historical unverified counts until reproduced.
gate: Equal data/model/hardware/concurrency and quality; include output decoding, embeddings, graph writes, cache misses and backlog. No claim of speed-up from prompt length alone.

title: One-call design is a target, not a hard observed total
finding: Confirmed: split mode and errors complicate counts; repair is proposed. A unified item list should not turn one invalid item into loss of the whole batch.
solution: Use per-item validation; bound attempts, elapsed time and output budget. Persist failure reason and retry eligibility. Guard against truncation; a cap must expose coverage loss or schedule remaining content rather than silently discard it.
gate: Malformed JSON, mixed valid/invalid items, oversized lists, timeouts and schema mismatch; report useful assertions per token and dropped coverage, not only parse success.

title: f-slot is one inconclusive quality result with high observed cost
finding: Register reports +1/−4 on 437, fired on 150; changes outside fired cases need attribution checks. Pre-I80 absolute results are contaminated; relative deltas are not automatically immune.
solution: Keep historical runs labelled; use clean pinned paired references, conversation-level uncertainty and per-slice losses. Separate adoption decision from general claims about all agentic retrieval. Pre-register non-inferiority margins and cost limits.
gate: All required blind sets present; matched manifests; repeated null controls estimate false adoption rate. Do not promise that a random seed swap can never pass a statistical gate.

title: Treat user examples as hypotheses, not new answer keys
finding: Scope includes all saved questions. Implicit country relation, likely book ownership, image-supported title and duration calculations require different evidence contracts.
solution: Join cited facts for multi-hop relations; distinguish likely from known ownership. Use external sources only for general world knowledge, never invent private history. Route unresolved visual evidence to an opt-in image extraction path; store asset hash and uncertainty. Compute durations from compatible endpoints with precision bounds.
gate: Benchmark mode obeys allowed tools; external-tool and text-only results are separate. Test both gains and regressions across all categories, not just the 13 examples. Preserve original gold and record disputed references separately.

title: Complete cells are not verified implementations
finding: All 15×57 survey rows and 15×23 prompt cells can be inventoried. Prompt instruction presence is not enforcement; snapshot scores do not certify current OSS code or cloud products.
solution: Track code/default/opt-in/doc/branch/measured independently; include commit, data/reader/judge/budget. Mark uninspected claims as inherited. Replace blanket best/fastest/no-other-engine language with scoped evidence.
gate: All evidence links and pins traceable; an independent reader can distinguish historical survey assertions from this review’s confirmed findings.

gaps: Wave A, G-P1, G-P3, G-P4, G-P6
title: CPU-testable does not mean quality-neutral
finding: Plan calls Wave A CPU-only with no screen. Language rules, length limits, date spans and repair alter model outputs or their interpretation.
evidence: gap_plan.json waves; G-P1, G-P3, G-P4, G-P6
solution: Separate deterministic infrastructure tests from extraction and downstream quality screens. Avoid universal hard 40-word limits that erase lists or conditions. Evaluate completeness and fidelity per fact type.
gate: CPU tests first; held-out extraction precision/recall and downstream non-inferiority before enabling quality-affecting changes. No guaranteed improvement for every individual question.

title: Implementation statuses have aged
finding: Read-time fact chain, event ledger and source lifting have code/config hooks; older register calls every hypothesis not implemented. A hook alone still does not implement the complete proposed solution.
solution: Use partial/built-off with named hooks and remaining work, separate from experimentally successful. Preserve the frozen per-question answers and scores; add a current-status overlay.
gate: All 25 historical hypotheses linked to the current plan and reviewed status; automated checks must not mistake existence of a symbol for full implementation.

title: Similarity thresholds are different mechanisms
finding: Name MinHash trigram Jaccard and embedding cosine are distinct. A 0.9 threshold is not transferable across them or across embedding models. Same name can refer to different entities.
solution: Preserve ambiguous entities; resolve with scoped type and context. Calibrate candidate generation and merge thresholds independently. Search contradictions by subject/predicate/time as well as high cosine similarity.
gate: Held-out alias/homonym pairs, negations and low-similarity contradictions; report false merges separately from missed merges. No auto-merge based only on shared spelling.

title: Graphiti call counts depend on the entry point
finding: Source checks confirm separate node/edge extraction on add_episode and combined extraction by default on bulk. Edge resolution skips dedupe when no candidates or when text/endpoints match verbatim; timestamps, attributes and unresolved identities add conditional calls.
solution: Pin version and entry point. Count extraction + unresolved-node resolution + eligible edge adjudications + timestamp/attribute/summary work, including retries. Borrow provenance and conditional resolution, not a fixed call-count claim. Repeated mentions can reuse an edge and append provenance; semantic dedup is not solely text identity.
gate: Trace counters by stage on the actual integration before claiming cost parity. Combined’s older embedded Graphiti snapshot is a separate version.

title: Failure modes must be distinguished
finding: Source checks: MemOS returns before raw deletion on a raised fine-transfer exception, but can fall through to deletion on empty results. Nemori can delete skipped small groups; semantic generation exceptions are swallowed while the episode may survive. This is narrower than all failures lose raw turns.
solution: Classify raised failure, swallowed failure, malformed reply, valid empty reply, size-based skip and partial commit. Retain raw sources and explicit derivation status. A validated empty extraction may be acknowledged as a no-op; do not retry valid empty windows forever.
gate: Fault fixtures for each outcome with documented source/episode/fact survival and bounded retry. Code-path analysis here is not an executed loss reproduction.

title: Stage, variant and deployment labels are required
finding: The records themselves say Mnemon’s raw record path has zero LLM calls and optional consolidation; its small answer context excludes auxiliary model reading. Memori prompt cells frequently describe legacy v2, while current extraction is hosted. The inherited one-call/example-free summary is not reliable.
evidence: mnemon.json extract.calls and token_economy; prompt_matrix.json F18 and Memori variants; memori.json
solution: Label OSS/cloud, current/legacy/experiment/host-agent and exact entry point per claim. Report answer tokens and auxiliary read tokens separately. 1,127 windows / 5,882 turns is segmentation density, not measured total calls per turn. Do not show one vendor score as the pinned code’s score.
gate: Full-path accounting includes split/repair, session close, sleep, planner, reranker and reader. Unknown hosted behaviour stays unknown. Prompt presence must not be conflated with storage semantics.

title: Untraced scope conditions must stay visible
finding: Claude flagged that an EverMemOS row ID omits app/project, but actual collision depends on entry-ID uniqueness and write semantics. Likewise, an erasure path does not certify all caches and derived views. These end-to-end claims were not reproduced in this review.
evidence: survey Claude F-11/F-12; engine Claude F6
solution: State conditional risks rather than proven exploits. Test identical IDs/text in separate tenants, source deletion after restart, and every derived projection/cache. Distinguish soft removal from hard erasure and retention policy.
gate: Isolation tests cover write/search/update/delete and cache hits. Erasure checks cover residual content plus lineage and scheduled jobs. Recheck current code before presenting historical security claims as current facts.

title: The synthesis and gap inventory drift
finding: The current plan has 41 gap cards. G-W32 appears in the synthesis but has no card in this plan snapshot. Five by-design IDs have no wave; that need not mean missing work.
evidence: synthesis.json section 7; gap_plan.json gaps and waves
solution: Keep an explicit unresolved cross-reference ledger. Treat G-W32 as a design candidate overlapping summary pointers/observation dedup, not an implemented or silently retired feature. Derive counts and require an explicit unscheduled/by-design reason.
gate: Validator reports dangling IDs, duplicate IDs, missing row evidence and incompatible variant claims. Resolve semantics manually rather than enforcing brittle keyword checks.
